anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet the two M12 connectors 'CAN Interface A' (J13) and 'CAN Interface B' (J17) carry an identical set of CAN data nets on pins 3/4/6 (NET0069, NET0020, NET0196); only the per-connector e-stop pin (pin 2: NET0062 vs NET0125) and the power/ESTOP pins differ. anomalies.expected: Per the specification the board provides two *isolated* CAN buses, CAN0 and CAN1, each driven by its own MCP2515 + isolated transceiver and broken out on its own M12 connector ('CAN Interface A' and 'CAN Interface B'). Each connector should therefore carry only that bus's CANH/CANL pair, keeping the two buses separate and galvanically isolated.

evidence.quote: J13 (CAN Interface A) pins: 3=NET0069, 4=NET0020, 6=NET0196; J17 (CAN Interface B) pins: 3=NET0069, 4=NET0020, 6=NET0196 (CAN BUS sheet, connector tiles)

anomalies.impact: CAN0 and CAN1 are merged onto both connectors, destroying the intended galvanic isolation between the two motor/actuator buses and forcing the two Odrive networks to share one bus; one transceiver's CAN line is left unconnected to any connector, so the second bus cannot communicate.
